chunks: What is a gyroscope / accelerometer?. The question: What is a gyroscope/accelerometer?
An accelerometer measures how hard a device is being pushed along each direction, which is the same as how quickly its speed is changing.
It also feels gravity, so it can tell which way is down. A gyroscope measures how fast the device is rotating. Neither one directly gives you position or angle.
Picture a small ball hanging on a spring inside a box.
When you speed the box forward, the ball lags behind and stretches the spring, and the stretch tells you how hard you accelerated.
Sitting still on a table, the ball still sags, because gravity pulls it. That is why an accelerometer at rest reads 1 g upward: the table pushes the box up.
In free fall the ball floats and the reading is zero. A gyroscope is different: it only reports how fast you are turning, like a speedometer for spinning.
The proof mass is held by a spring; when the case accelerates the mass shifts by x = a/ω0², changing the gaps (and so the capacitances) to the fixed electrodes.
Real devices use many interdigitated comb fingers to get usable capacitance in a few hundred micrometres.
g: the pull of Earth's gravity, about 9. 81 m/s². Readings are often given in g. MEMS: micro-electro-mechanical system, a tiny moving machine etched into a silicon chip.
Proof mass: the tiny mass in the chip that lags behind when the chip is pushed, like the ball. Angular rate: how fast something rotates, in degrees per second.
Adding it up over time gives an angle. Axis: one of three directions (x, y, z) the sensor measures along.
Lay a 3-axis accelerometer flat on a table. It reads 0 g on x, 0 g on y and 1 g on z (up). Stand it on its edge, and the 1 g moves to a different axis.
That is how a phone knows which way is up. Now spin a gyroscope a quarter turn (90 degrees) in one second. It reads 90 degrees per second while turning, and 0 once you stop.
"An accelerometer measures specific force: a tiny MEMS proof mass on springs shifts when the case accelerates and the capacitance change is read out.
At rest it reads 1 g up and in free fall zero, which lets it find the gravity direction.
A gyroscope measures angular rate: a vibrating mass feels a Coriolis force when the chip rotates, and the sideways motion is proportional to the rate.
To get an angle from a gyro you integrate, which drifts."
